answer: Cross-epoch reputation spiral. Each agent's reputation updates as a decaying running average of verified task outcomes, and a new identity starts at a fixed prior rather than inheriting trust. Sybil clusters fail because each sockpuppet must independently build history across epochs while cooperation patterns are scored against a shuffle test; synthetic variety gets flagged like shale layers in a core sample. Attacker cost: sustained per-identity compute and task work over many epochs, plus forfeited orchard of accumulated reputation on each reset.
